author: GamingBolt
description:
The 14th century had its share of conflicts, but very few could match the longevity of the Hundred Years' War. It lasted over 116 years, waged across three lengthy periods. The first ranged from 1337 to 1360, but even with this massive clash, something else overtook society at large: the Black Death. A plague spread by rats, exacerbated by filthy living conditions at the time. Its impact was utterly devastating, with tens of millions dead.

Few video games have really delved into this era, and for good reason. Between the persecution, the rise of humanism, and the development of medicine, it was a dark, depressing time where death could come from anywhere at any time. And no one was safe. So, taking that setting and portraying it from the perspective of two children, ages 15 and 5? “Horrified” doesn't even begin to describe how your average parent/uncle/aunt/older sibling would have felt.

But A Plague Tale: Innocence was different. It didn't go overboard with the horror or exploit it
title: A Plague Tale: Innocence - The Full Story - Before You Play Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy

author: GamingBolt
description:
Madden NFL 27 is flashy. Unfortunately, in the first year after that trade, my Bears missed the playoffs, and then we entered salary cap hell that caused me to lose some great players and soft rebuild. Likewise, Madden 27 provides a clear, flashy upgrade to the Franchise mode both in how it looks and feels to play, particularly because of how much more enticing it is to handle off-the-field activities. 

Outside of that, though, the rest of the package hasn’t moved much aside from some on-field tweaks and some new positions in Superstar, which is now inundated with single-player microtransactions. Madden tries to do something big this year, and though parts of it certainly improve, I can say from experience now that the flashiest move doesn’t always make the whole thing better.
title: EA Sports Madden NFL 27 Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
GTA 6 is still nearly three months away but Rockstar’s already getting the conversation started with a very interesting gameplay reveal on Netflix. We had some thoughts about that, but that was before Take Two’s Strauss Zelnick gave some very insightful statements to various sources that made us rethink our original position. 

Where we once thought Netflix might have been eager to debut the reveal ahead of Rockstar’s other channels, we’re now suspecting that things could be more than that? Curious? Good. Join us as we take a look at what might be cooking behind the curtain of a much-awaited reveal for one of 2026’s biggest titles, and try to take educated guesses about the methods to Rockstar’s latest madness.
title: GTA 6: Why Is Netflix Getting The Gameplay Reveal First?
